chunks: He presented to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) some of the sermons of his father; until when he reached a passage in it, he said to him: 'Stop, and be silent.'

Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no leeway for you regarding what comes upon you from what you do not know, except to refrain from it, to verify carefully, and to refer it back to the Imams of Guidance, until they guide you in it toward the right path, and they dispel from you the blindness in it, and they make the truth known to you in it.'
God the Exalted said: 'So ask the People of the Reminder if you do not know' [16:43].

key_terms.أَئِمَّةِ الْهُدَى: Imams of Guidance — the divinely appointed Imams of the Ahlulbayt
key_terms.أَهْلَ الذِّكْرِ: People of the Reminder — Quranic title applied here to the Imams
key_terms.التَّثَبُّتُ: deliberate verification — careful, unhurried confirmation before acting
key_terms.الْكَفُّ: restraint — refraining from judgment or speech on unknown matters

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq (AS) teach in al-Kafi about referring matters of religious uncertainty to the Imams of Guidance?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) instructs that when a believer encounters a matter they do not understand, the only permissible response is al-kaff (refraining), al-tathabbut (deliberate verification), and al-radd (referral) to the Imams of Guidance. The hadith concludes with Quran 16:43, applied here to identify the Imams as the 'People of the Reminder (Ahl al-Dhikr),' establishing their exclusive authority as the proper reference in all matters of religious uncertainty.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Hamza Bin Al Tayyar that, 
‘He presented to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> some of the sermons of his father, until when he reached a subject from it, he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Stop, and be silent’.

Then Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no leeway for you regarding what comes to you from what you do not know except to pause at that, and affirming, and referring it back to the Imams<sup>asws</sup> of the Guidance, until they<sup>asws</sup> deliver to you the purpose (of it), and they<sup>asws</sup> isolate from you the blindness in (that where you are going), and they<sup>asws</sup> make you recognise the truth in it.
Allahazwj the Exalted Said [16:43] so ask the People of the (Zikr) (Reminder) if you do not know’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad has narrated from Ahmad from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from Hamza ibn al-Tayyar the following. “(Imam) abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) said, ‘In the case of what may come to you and you have no knowledge of its veracity you can do nothing but to hold and verify and refer it to the Imams of guidance so that he would show the way of justice in it and enlighten you in the darkness and introduce to you the truth.
Allah, the Most High has said, “Ask those who know about the heavenly Books if you do not know about this.”
